A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HBoP. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: V1 reports original caption-generation evaluations on MSCOCO, Flickr30K and NoCaps, alongside semantic-integrity evaluations and visual analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds IoU sensitivity, direct-cropping comparisons and segmentation-runtime measurements.

M1.justification: Appendix D.4 introduces an evaluated HBoP variant using FastSAM instead of SAM. The main hierarchy construction, embedding selection and BLIP captioning procedure remain unchanged; expanded extraction explanations do not establish further algorithm changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate image captioning on the MSCOCO Karpathy 5k split, Flickr30K 1k split and NoCaps 4.5k validation set. The added comparisons do not introduce new datasets, populations or task requirements.

E2.justification: V2 adds the Crop baseline, which captions directly cropped segmented regions using BLIP, in Table 3 on MSCOCO and Flickr30K. Comparator membership in the retained benchmark, semantic-integrity and relevance-correlation comparisons is unchanged.

E3.justification: New experiments vary IoU across 0.1, 0.4 and 0.8 and measure segmentation time per image and captioning time per caption. Section 4 newly specifies two global and three regional captions, but Appendix C.3.1 retains v1's one-global/five-regional description. The reported sampling descriptions conflict, so an actual sampling change or rerun cannot be established.

E4.justification: V2 substantially expands diagnostic evidence with IoU-threshold sensitivity (Table 2), a cropping control testing the benefit of embedding sampling (Table 3), and SAM/FastSAM efficiency analysis (Table 5). These address parameter sensitivity, the central design choice and computational overhead beyond v1's retained correlations and qualitative examples.

E5.justification: The semantic-integrity uncertainty values are identical in v1 Table 2 and v2 Table 4, and the regression significance reporting in Appendix D.1 is retained. V2 introduces no seed counts, repeated-run information or uncertainty estimates for its new analyses.

E6.justification: All original benchmark and semantic-integrity values remain unchanged, but v2 adds substantive findings on sensitivity, cropping and computational cost. Div-2 decreases from 0.735 to 0.666 as IoU increases from 0.1 to 0.8; the MSCOCO Crop baseline scores 52.03 SBERT versus HBoP's 56.30; segmentation takes 5.43 seconds/image with SAM versus 0.18 with FastSAM. Table 3 also duplicates Flickr30K BLIP(+NS) Div-2 as 0.387, inconsistent with 0.384 in the retained Table 1.

T1.justification: The mask-selection, embedding-extraction and caption-generation equations, together with the PCD definition, are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, proofs or derivations appear.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the central claim that training-free hierarchical embedding sampling with BLIP improves caption diversity while maintaining relevance and approaching larger-model performance. The abstract's reported diversity scores and the conclusion's contribution claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations involving full-image context in last-layer embeddings, overlapping masks causing repetition, and segmentation overhead. It newly treats SBERT as a human-quality proxy and infers resistance to SAM errors. Section 6 adds the limitation that factual diversity does not necessarily capture cultural interpretations requiring external knowledge.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-access link and clarifies the extraction layer, projection of regional clusters onto patches, concatenation and padding. It also reports segmentation and captioning times. The main backbone, cluster counts and default IoU threshold were already documented in v1.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds positioning against region-based representations and caption-quality research, citing Shlapentokh-Rothman et al. and Chen et al. It removes the explicit methodological criticism of PnP-VQA, while retaining that work elsewhere. Additional citations support efficient segmentation, cultural-diversity limitations and other contextual points.

P1.justification: V2 makes targeted rewrites in the introduction, related work, results and limitations, expands explanatory footnotes, and moves semantic-integrity discussion into Appendix C.3.3. Author information and acknowledgements are updated. The overall narrative structure and most appendix prose remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds three compact tables and relocates the semantic-integrity table from the main text to the appendix. Figure 2 and Table 1 receive revised captions, and the LLM column heading changes. All five figures retain their visual content; the principal page-layout conventions remain.

improvement.justification: The cropping control, threshold analysis and runtime measurements provide useful support for previously untested design and efficiency arguments. The code link and implementation explanations also improve reproducibility information. These gains are limited by the unresolved caption-sampling contradiction, the duplicated baseline-value inconsistency, and claims about SAM-error tolerance and FastSAM quality without corresponding validation. Overall, v2 modestly strengthens the paper.
